subject: Aligning throughput targets to model quantization & fallback routing
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Grace Occonnor <grace@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 04 May 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Aligning throughput targets to model quantization & fallback routing

Samir / Alyssa —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap of what we heard and the concrete next steps so we can align engineering + procurement on the same page. I captured the parts that matter for the infra & SRE teams.

Key pain / goals you shared:
- High QPS peaks (spikes to ~1.2k qps for short windows) with strict 95th-p99 latency targets of ~150-200ms for synchronous user journeys.
- Cost pressure: want to avoid provisioning large reserved fleets for 95% of traffic; prefer burst + fallback model variants rather than worst-case provisioning.
- Model quality must be at parity with your current fp16 model for clinical summarization; occasional fallback to a faster quantized variant is acceptable if we can route gracefully.
- Audit/logging requirements: full request/response audit trail (30d retention), and integration with your Splunk instance.

Technical constraints we noted:
- Average prompt length: 220 tokens; tail of requests up to 1k tokens during some workflows.
- Current model: Novus uses a custom finetuned 34B decoder model (fp16) in prod. They are open to 8-bit quantized variants for cost but want a plan for accuracy/regression monitoring.
- Network: VPC peering available; preference for Private deployment (dedicated) in us-west2.

Our proposed approach (high level):
1) Two-tier model routing: primary fp16 model for baseline, fallback 8-bit quantized variant for bursts and degraded SLOs.
2) Smart routing policy: route by latency budget + token ceiling; short requests (<400 tokens) favor quantized variant when we detect burst pressure.
3) Autoscaled dedicated pool with burst capacity and cross-region fallback to keep tail latency under 250ms during peak surges.
4) Prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts (clinical templates) to reduce cost and latency for hot paths.

Immediate next steps we agreed on:
- I will share a draft MOP (mutual action plan) and a sample SLO table capturing p50/p95/p99 targets + example loads. (attached)
- Karthik to propose an initial topology sketch (GPU sizing, batch targets) and quantization profile options by EOD tomorrow.
- You (Samir) to confirm compliance constraints (audit log retention, KMS) and share a redacted sample request distribution if possible.

Attachments: Novus_SLOs.csv (draft SLO table), MUTUAL_ACTION_PLAN_Novus.docx (skeleton MOP).

If that aligns I’ll schedule a 45m follow-up with Karthik and Grace for Wed to walk the topology.

Thanks —
Priyom

Priyom,

Appreciate the tidy recap — this matches our notes. A couple clarifications before the topology call: 

1) The 1.2k qps spike is observed during patient intake windows for ~8–12 minutes; sustained baseline is ~120 qps. Peak requests are roughly 70% < 300 tokens, but the long-tail (up to 1k tokens) is important for batch summarization jobs (can be async).

2) For compliance: we do require HSM-backed KMS for any keys used in private deployment. Audit logs need to be exportable to our Splunk via forwarder (30d).

3) On quantization: we can tolerate a small accuracy delta for non-critical summarization flows; critical clinical outputs must stay on fp16. Need a clear A/B/regression plan.

We’ll attach a small anonymized request histogram (should help sizing) in the next note. Re: scheduling — Wed afternoon PT works; can you propose 3 slots?

Thanks,
Samir

Looping in a quick topology sketch and sizing notes (summary inline) — will bring diagrams to the call.

Summary / initial sizing assumptions:
- Baseline pool: 8x A100-80GB equivalent (serve fp16 model), targeted for steady ~120 qps with 5–10ms network overhead and batching tuned to 16 tokens avg.
- Burst pool: 4x T4-like instances running the 8-bit quantized model to absorb short spikes and keep p95 under 200ms for short prompts.
- Cross-region fallback: replicate minimal serving group in us-central to accept overflow at higher latency (<= 250–300ms) if us-west2 capacity exhausted.
- Batching strategy: dynamic batching with per-request latency budgets and max batch windows = 12ms for low-latency paths; larger windows for async jobs.

Quantization approach:
- Try 8-bit (nf4/awq) on a representative slice of your weights; run microbench with 2000 sample prompts (we can do this in your private env).
- Define a regression suite (precision metrics on clinical classification & ROUGE for summarization) — Grace will own test harness and alert thresholds.

Operational asks for Novus:
- Provide anonymized request histogram and example prompt templates (Samir)
- KMS/HSM contact & Splunk forwarding details for audit export (security)

I’ve attached the draft SLO CSV Priyom sent and a short script (ops sizing notes) as text in the MOP doc.

-Karthik
